messages:
Maya: Taking over primary for the night shift. Quick context: we're seeing a recurring tail-latency spike on /v1/generate (hosted API) starting ~02:45 UTC. Root cause unknown. Current quick mitigations I triggered: rolled model from v1.3.2 -> v1.2.9 at 03:10 UTC, enabled prefix/KV caching for top customers, bumped batch timeout to 40ms. Posting handoff so runtime/infra/support/security routing is clear. :rotating_light:

PagerDuty: Incident PD-867 assigned to Maya — Severity: P1 — alert: elevated 95th/99th latency for generate across us-west. See incident channel #inc-867.

Liam: I’m taking secondary. Plan: check runtime KV cache miss rates, KV eviction logs, and slot contention. I’ll start by tailing runtime logs and checking the batching histograms. Runbook here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-inference — main commands:

```
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime -c runtime --tail=200
redis-cli -h redis.cluster.svc.info INFO stats | egrep "keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses"
# check batching histograms from monitoring: /dashboards/runtime/batching
```

Jen: infra on-call for tonight is the ops-night rotation (pager: ops-pd). If you see node-level GPU OOMs, driver crashes, or AZ flaps -> page infra immediately (PD service: infra-pd). For mesos/k8s node pressure I want the pod eviction logs and node metrics (nvidia-smi, dmesg). If you need a manual GPU reboot we should coordinate to avoid double-restarts.

Sam: Security only gets paged for auth anomalies, data exfil, or anything that looks like credential compromise. Perf issues generally stay with runtime/infra unless we see abnormal egress rates or suspicious queries. For security page: security-pd and add the tag `[data-exfil]`.

Maya: Noted coverage gap: infra secondary will be short-handed between 04:00-06:00 UTC (ops-night has only one person that window). I've pinged ops manager to be on standby; if we hit additional node failures escalate to ops manager (Jen will share contact). Avoid escalation unless severity P0.

Liam: Found higher KV miss ratio on the hot prefixes (~6x baseline) and a burst of cache invalidations at 03:07. Looks like cache evictions correlate with the model rollback traffic. I'll increase cache TTL for those prefixes and throttle the invalidations if the runtime supports it. Also seeing a spike in concurrent connections to runtime workers — possible batching pressure.

Maya: Good. If increasing TTL doesn't hold, consider temporarily disabling model-variant routing (sticky to smaller variants) to reduce cross-model cold starts. Also, I left a note in the runbook under "temporary mitigations".

Jen: If you need to move requests away from affected nodes, tag the node and cordon/drain with caution. Cordoning will trigger autoscaler and may not be immediate. Commands: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. If you're unsure ping me before drain.

Liam: Understood. I'll try TTL and request routing changes first. If that doesn't help within 15m, I'll escalate to infra for node-level intervention.

Support Bot: Creating internal ticket for affected customers (top 5 by QPS). Will also post a short status update to status.redwood.ai and add a note to the support queue.

Maya: Customer impact assessment: ~3% of requests see >2s added tail-latency, disproportionally affects a handful of enterprise customers on long-context workloads. No data loss or auth issues observed. Support: prioritize those enterprise customers and offer mitigation guidance (reduce max_tokens or use shorter context) while we stabilize.

Sam: Security confirmation: no suspicious egress seen in last 30m. If anyone sees unexpected S3 or external IP traffic spike, tag security immediately.

Liam: Running the TTL bump now and gating the invalidation job. Will report metrics in 5m.

(oncall bot): Handoff checklist reminder: primary declared (Maya), secondary declared (Liam), runbook linked, PD escalation routes confirmed (infra-pd, security-pd, support-pd), status page action assigned.

Maya: Also — cross-team routing rules we agreed on: runtime team owns model-serving code/containers/batching/kv cache; infra owns node/GPU/host/network; security owns auth/egress/suspicious activity; support owns customer comms and SLA notifications. If an alert contains both perf and auth signals, page both runtime and security.

Liam: Metrics update: 10m after TTL bump - 95th latency dropped ~30%, 99th down ~18%. Still above baseline. If this trend continues we'll avoid infra cordons. If it regresses, escalating to infra for node-level investigation.

Jen: Ops manager contact (in case of P0 or coverage escalation): jen-smith-manager@redwood.internal — ops manager asked to be pinged only if node restarts or AZ issues.

Maya: Noting a manual step that helped earlier: temporarily pin traffic to v1.2.9 for top 3 customers. Pattern: cold starts from model variant rotation + cache churn. Might be worth a follow-up to Improve model-rotation TTLs in Optimize.

Support Bot: Tickets created and account teams notified. Will post a status page update in 10 minutes if metrics don't return to baseline.

Liam: Handoff acceptance — I’m on until 05:30 UTC. I will take lead; Maya, happy to have you on standby for 30 minutes if you want to remain for context.

Maya: I’ll stay for 20. If things look stable in 30m I’ll sign off. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
